newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 11.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
BJP SEEKS TIE UP WITH BAHUJAN SAMAJ PARTY IN UTTAR PRADESH

The Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is understood to have reached an understanding with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) to form a coalition government in India's Uttar Pradesh state following local elections. According to the agreement, the government will be headed by BSP leader Mayawati. The newspaper said the coalition formula was worked out in a meeting between Mayawati and senior BJP leader and former prime minister Atal Behari Vajpayee.
The Economic Times

PORT REGULATORY BODY, PRIVATE PARTICIPATION APPROVED The Indian cabinet approved the setting up of an independent port regulatory authority to fix and revise port tariffs. The legislation will be placed before parliament in coming months. The Cabinet also approved revised guidelines framed by the Surface Transport Ministry to facilitate private sector investment in 11 major ports. Under the guidelines, construction and operation of additional assets in the ports have been allowed.
CENTRAL BANK PLANS TO RAISE $400 MLN

The Reserve Bank Of India (RBI), the central bank, will for the first time raise a foreign currency loan from the commercial market. RBI plans to raise a $400 million, 10-year syndicated loan through its wholly-owned subsidiary, Bhartiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Pvt Ltd. The loan is being viewed as a precursor to the government launching a sovereign loan programme in the overseas commercial market.
COGENTRIX GETS APPROVAL FOR COUNTER-GURANTEE

Counter-guarantees for the Cogentrix power project in Mangalore have been approved. The counter-guarantees will cover payments of capacity and energy charges for the proposed 1,000 MW thermal power project. This is the fourth project to receive counter-guarantees from the Government.
OECF SAID TO PICK UP EQUITY IN CORE PROJECTS

The Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund (OECF) of Japan will pick up equity in Indian infrastructure projects involving Japanese corporates. Sources said Marubeni, Sumitomo and Mitsui had approached OECF for equity participation in their Indian ventures. These corporates are currently engaged in talks for joint venture projects in the power and transportation sectors.
APPROVALS FOR BORROWINGS WORTH $6 BLN NOT UTILISED

External commercial borrowing approvals worth almost $6 billion have not been utilised. Most companies which obtained approvals have not been able to raise the necessary funds. This is attributed mainly to a deteriorating view on Indian credit risk and bad market conditions. Of the approximate $7 billion worth of approvals granted for the current fiscal, barely $1.2 billion were drawn, finance ministry officials said.
Financial Express
REVAMP PACKAGE FOR STATE-OWNED FIRMS

A capital restructuring package has been finalised for four public sector enterprises -- Bharat Yantra Nigam Ltd, Bharat Bhari Udyog Nigam Ltd, Cement Corporation of India and Hindustan Machine Tools Ltd. The scheme, finalised by the industry ministry, envisages privatisation and restructuring, including closure of loss-making units of these companies and joint ventures with leading domestic or foreign collaborators giving them stakes of up to 75 percent.
Business Standard
DIVESTMENT PANEL ACCEPTS LIST OF PUBLIC SECTOR UNITS

The Disinvestment Commission has accepted a list of 40 public sector units (PSUs) referred to it by the core group of secretaries. The PSUs include Air India, Steel Authority of India, Gas Authority of India, Indian Tourism Development Corporation and National Thermal Power Corporation. Public sector units under the administrative jurisdiction of the industry ministry were excluded from the list.
AUTOMATIC APPROVAL FOR 50 PCT FOREIGN EQUITY STAKE PROPOSED

The Ministry of Mines may allow foreign equity of up to 51 percent in the mining sector on a case-to-case basis. The ministry may also propose automatic clearance of proposals with foreign equity up to 50 percent. This does not conform with the industry ministry, which proposed automatic clearance for 51 percent foreign equity in the mining sector.
UTI BANK EQUITY ISSUE VIA BOOK-BUILDING

UTI Bank, promoted by Unit Trust of India, Life Insurance Corporation, General Insurance Corporation and others, plans to float its maiden equity issue through the book-building process. This is the first equity issue in the country to raise funds this way. Following the issue, UTI Bank's paid up capital will rise from 1.15 billion rupees to three billion rupees.
AMOCO PLANS INVESTMENT IN PETROCHEM, LNG PROJECTS

The $30 billion U.S.-based Amoco Corporation plans to invest in a petrochemicals and a gas project. Amoco was keen to invest in India despite its recent decision to scrap plans to invest $1 billion in a methane gas project. Under the scrapped project, Amoco was to have extracted gas from coal fields in Bihar and West Bengal.
The Observer

INDIA PLANS TO APPEAL TO WTO OVER ANTI-DUMPING DUTY India plans to appeal to the World Trade Organisation against the European Union (EU) over the imposition of anti-dumping duty on Indian unbleached fabric. The textile ministry believes the EU's decision to levy the anti-dumping duty on such imports is unfair. The European Commission had earlier imposed an anti-dumping duty between 15 and 20 percent on the import of unbleached fabric from India, China, Indonesi, Turkey and Pakistan.
Business Line
STATE PARTICIPATION CLAUSE MAY GO

The Petroleum Ministry plans to scrap the mandatory state participation clause for its next offer inviting private sector bids for exploration acreages. Pending clearance of the new exploration lincensing policy, the ministry has proposed to invite fresh bids for exploration acreages. The ministry has identified about 40 blocks for the purpose.
